audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir/Skill for rows 0-3 while the whys directly under it said Akshan wins all four. The packet chart is Akshan x4 then Vladimir x3.
audit.why: The page contradicted itself on who wins the first four rows, and the prose was the correct half.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 flipped to Akshan in matched full/content pairs with 4/10 ratings; row 4 flipped to Vladimir where his first-item sustain and the pooled Comeuppance turn the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns and no ranges — 'his range' was never quantified and the ultimate window was never priced.
audit.why: Avengerang is 850 range against Transfusion's 600; Heroic Swing 18/16.5/15/13.5/12; Comeuppance 100/85/70 against a 28s Sanguine Pool. That arithmetic is the whole matchup, exactly as the mirror audit found.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into phases[0], phases[1], phases[3], phases[4], spikes[1], early and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate errors. (1) 'Going Rogue's grievous-wound passive' — Going Rogue is his W, and Riot's passive text (Dirty Fighting) grants bonus damage and a shield every third hit, no Grievous Wounds anywhere. (2) 'his W swing' and 'Use W to swing away' put Heroic Swing in the wrong slot twice. (3) Camouflage and terrain were never mentioned.
audit.why: Going Rogue is camouflage and Vladimir has no reveal in his kit, so Control Wards and a sweeper are mandatory. Heroic Swing anchors into terrain and can cut a dashless champion's retreat — Flash is for the wall, not the damage. Sanguine Pool's 2s untargetability eats the entire Comeuppance volley.
audit.corrected: Passive renamed to Dirty Fighting and described as a shield; swing moved to Heroic Swing (E); camouflage/vision and terrain-retreat written in.

edits.before: Q-drain on cooldown — you trade HP like a loan shark. Identify how Akshan contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Avengerang out-ranges everything you have, 850 to Transfusion's 600. Soak XP, last-hit, and take the chip instead of stepping up.

edits.before: Pool answers his single biggest button — save it for exactly that. Only take the trade when Akshan's Heroic Swing is down.
edits.after: His ranged poke keeps you off the wave and you have no answer yet. Sanguine Pool is 28s — never spend it on Avengerang chip.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Akshan must walk into your range.
edits.after: Heroic Swing needs terrain to anchor — hold the open lane centre so he cannot swing in and cut your retreat.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heroic Swing's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still his: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and his harass outpaces your sustain. Farm safe and bank XP toward your first item.

edits.before: Hemoplague + empowered Q turns mid-game fights into resets. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Akshan's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Six turns it: pool the Comeuppance volley and its 100s cooldown leaves him with nothing while Hemoplague heals you back up.

edits.before: Level 3 stays his as W disengage dodges your Transfusion trades.
edits.after: Level 3 stays his — Heroic Swing (E) swings him out of your Transfusion.

edits.before: Akshan dominates levels 1-3 with ranged Avengerang poke and Going Rogue's grievous-wound passive; you can't answer his range, so soak XP, use Transfusion on the wave, and take the chip.
edits.after: Akshan dominates levels 1-3 with 850-range Avengerang poke and a Dirty Fighting shield on every third hit; you cannot answer that range, so soak XP, Transfusion the wave, and take the chip.

edits.before: He keeps the poke lead through levels 4-5 but the moment your first AP item and Crimson Pact haste land the range gap closes and your sustain outpaces his harass.
edits.after: He keeps the poke lead through 4-5; carry a Control Ward and sweep, because Going Rogue is camouflage and nothing in your kit reveals him. Your first AP item closes the gap.

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang plus Going Rogue passive shreds you at range, and his W swing lets him disengage your Transfusion; his early ranged poke keeps you off the wave through the whole first phase.
edits.after: Akshan's Avengerang plus a Dirty Fighting shield every third hit wins the range war, and Heroic Swing (E) anchors on terrain to swing him out of your Transfusion; his poke keeps you off the wave all phase.

edits.before: Comeuppance is a long-range execute that punishes you low, but if you Pool the channel you dodge the whole thing and can walk him down after.
edits.after: Comeuppance is a 100s missing-health volley; Sanguine Pool's 2s untargetability eats all of it, and then he has nothing for a minute and a half.

edits.before: Poke you off the wave with Avengerang and Going Rogue
edits.after: Poke you off the wave with Avengerang and Dirty Fighting

edits.before: Use W to swing away from your Transfusion lock
edits.after: Use Heroic Swing to break your Transfusion lock

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1, anchors on terrain and can cut your retreat — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage. - Comeuppance: 100s; pool the volley. - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, never on chip. - Hemoplague: 120s, kill windows only.

notes: The packet suspectName was right for the wrong reason: 'Going Rogue' is a real ability, but attributing a grievous-wound passive to it is doubly wrong — Going Rogue is the W, and Dirty Fighting (P) grants a shield, not anti-heal. Worth grepping the Vladimir content file for other 'grievous-wound passive' claims.
